content:
Since iOS 5 in 2011, iPhone and iPad have featured a built-in Notification Center, allowing users to centrally view notifications from various apps in chronological order.

Starting with iOS 27, Apple has made significant changes to the way users access Notification Center on iPhone and iPad.

iOS 27 is currently in beta, with the first two versions handling things slightly differently. However, all eight developer betas released so far indicate that this change will officially launch this month—even though I personally would prefer to revise it.

Siri AI replaces the large downward swipe gesture from the top edge of iPhone and iPad

By default, the way to open Notification Center on iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 remains unchanged. However, once Siri AI is enabled, a key swipe gesture on iPhone and iPad will be modified.

After enabling Siri AI, one way to invoke Siri AI is by swiping down from the center of the top edge of the iPhone or iPad screen. This gesture was previously used to open Notification Center.

With Siri AI enabled, users can still access Notification Center by swiping down from the top-left corner. Notifications now slide in with an animation from the top-left corner. This is designed to draw users' attention to the relatively small trigger area for Notification Center.

Apple has clearly prioritized Siri AI access in iOS 27, with most of the top edge area dedicated to invoking the new Siri experience.

The last time Apple changed the way to access Notification Center was with the iPhone X, when Control Center was switched from a swipe-up gesture from the bottom to a swipe-down gesture from the top-right corner. Apple subsequently unified this experience across all devices.

Notifications are now located in the top-left corner

Now it's Notification Center's turn to be "pushed into a corner." Particularly in iPadOS 27 beta 1, the area above the home screen app icons is almost entirely used for invoking Siri AI. If you turn off the display of AM/PM or the date, the area available for opening Notification Center actually shrinks.

Top comment posted by mz4srmsr

I've always swiped from the top-left corner to check notifications—I never knew you could swipe from the middle 😂 Seems like I'm not affected?

Apple made improvements in iPadOS 27 beta 2, dividing more uniform zones on both sides, each approximately the width of two columns of apps. The left side is for Notification Center, the right side for Control Center, and the rest is used for invoking Siri.

After 15 years of muscle memory, whether this change is worthwhile or needs to be reconsidered will take time to determine. Meanwhile, initial reactions to Apple's new Siri AI system have been quite positive. The phrase "Siri is finally useful" will also take time for everyone to get used to.

After months of using this new gesture, I would definitely turn it off if the system provided a setting to disable it. Since there is currently no option to disable the swipe-down-from-top-center gesture for invoking Siri, the only solution is to build new muscle memory and avoid the center position.

iOS 27 is currently available in developer and public beta versions, with the official release expected this month.
